overall: As of 1:00 PM ET, Atlanta is sitting at 75.2°F — the running max for the day — and still actively warming at +1.8°F/hr with a relatively comfortable dewpoint of 53.6°F and moderate winds of 11.5 mph. forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is weak: ECMWF (75.2°F) has already been matched by observed temps at just 1 PM, suggesting it is verifying on the low side or has already peaked, while GFS (78.0°F) and NBM (76.1°F) leave room for further warming. max_temp_prediction: With the current warming rate of +1.8°F/hr at 1 PM and Atlanta typically peaking between 3–4 PM ET in early June, there is likely 1.5–2 more hours of meaningful heating, though the rate should decelerate as the afternoon progresses. Accounting for decelerating velocity, moderate winds limiting surface heating, and the NBM/GFS bracketing at 76.1–78.0°F, a final high in the 76.5–77.5°F range seems most probable. Confidence is moderate — the ECMWF already verifying and low ensemble probabilities for the upper bins argue against a GFS-level outcome.
